data.title: A Camera That Fits With You: Fujifilm Introduces instax Pal 2™ Digital Camera
data.description:
A Camera That Fits With You: Fujifilm Introduces instax Pal 2™ Digital Camera

Second iteration in popular instax Pal™ series features new upgrades with a classic analog look and feel

FUJIFILM North America Corporation, Imaging Division, today announced the launch of the next generation of its unique, ultra-portable instax Pal™ digital camera series - instax Pal 2™ digital camera (hereafter Pal 2). Pal 2 brings a host of new features to the Pal lineup, like an optical viewfinder and new filters and shooting modes.

“When we introduced the original Pal in 2024, some consumers weren’t sure what to make of it,” said Bing Liem, division president, Imaging Division, FUJIFILM North America Corporation. “Its uniqueness wasn’t for some, while others felt it was a perfect go-anywhere camera and loved the overall image-making process that makes Pal different from other cameras. When designing Pal 2, we gathered extensive customer feedback on the original Pal. And with its new look, reminiscent of a classic analog camera, complete with an optical viewfinder, and the ability to send/post images digitally or print images via instax™ smartphone printers or any of our Evo hybrid cameras, Pal 2 puts options in the palm of your hand.”

The free, downloadable instax Pal™ app lets the user’s smartphone act as a remote shutter for hands-free photography. The app also lets users store and transfer their photos via Bluetooth®, while the built-in USB Type-C connector on the camera allows users to connect their smartphone directly to transfer photos into the app. Users can also review their image before transferring via Pal 2’s 1.0-inch LCD Screen on the top of the camera.

Users can make their photos personal with any of Pal 2’s five filter themes, each with six unique effects. Options also include the ability to switch between instax™ mini, SQUARE, or WIDE instant film and frameless formats before adding filters, text, and stickers.

Pal 2 includes instax Animation™ shooting mode – a new way to capture 10 frames and turn them into a playful, flipbook-style animation. Switching modes is quick and intuitive, making it easy to move from still images to animations. To print, users can choose their favorite shot and transfer it directly to any compatible, connected instax™ smartphone printer or hybrid instant camera (sold separately).

Main Feature Recap:

  • Palm-sized design, designed for ages 13+
  • Pal 2 does not print photos - users can print images using instax™ Link series smartphone printers, instax mini LiPlay™ or instax mini Evo™ devices (sold separately). Free smartphone download of the app relating to the applicable instax™ device required. instax™ instant film required for image printing (sold separately). Prints photos in instax™ mini, SQUARE or WIDE formats.
  • Authentic Optical Viewfinder
  • 1.0-inch LCD Screen
  • Camera angle adjustment accessory included
  • Five filter themes, each with six unique effects
  • Download of free instax Pal™ app required for use
  • Holds up to 100 photos at a time before required transfer to free, downloadable instax Pal™ app
  • instax Animation™ shooting mode
  • Wireless Bluetooth® 5.1 smartphone connectivity
  • Built-in USB Type-C connector
  • Accepts microSD Card (not included)
  • Includes USB Type-C Cable, Hand Strap, Camera Angle Adjustment Accessory and 1-Year Limited Warranty

Pricing and Availability

instax Pal 2™ digital camera is expected to be available late September 2026 at a Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price of $169.95 USD and $219.99 CAD. Pal 2 will be available in sleek Black or stylish White color options. For more information, please visit https://www.instaxus.com/cameras/instax-pal-2-digital-camera/.

About Fujifilm

FUJIFILM North America Corporation, a marketing subsidiary of FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation, consists of five operating divisions. The Imaging Division provides consumer and commercial photographic products and services, including silver halide consumables; inkjet consumables; digital printing equipment, along with service and support; personalized photo products fulfillment; film; one-time-use cameras; and the popular instax™ line of instant cameras, smartphone printers, instant film, and accessories. The Electronic Imaging Division markets its GFX System and X Series lines of mirrorless digital cameras, lenses, and accessories to provide a variety of content creation solutions for both still and moving imagery. The Optical Devices Division provides optical lenses for the broadcast, cinematography, closed circuit television, videography, and industrial markets, and also markets binoculars and other optical imaging solutions. The Business Innovation Division offers a full lineup of digital print and toner technologies focused on enabling the digital transformation of businesses and print shops with its offerings of multifunction printers, digital inkjet presses, production toner printers, software, and more. The Industrial Products Division delivers new products derived from Fujifilm technologies including data storage tape products, including OEM and FUJIFILM Ultrium LTO cartridges, desalination solutions, microfilters and gas separation membranes.

For more information, please visit https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region, go to https://x.com/fujifilmus to follow Fujifilm on X, or go to https://www.facebook.com/FujifilmAmerica to Like Fujifilm on Facebook.

FUJIFILM Corporation is a subsidiary of FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation. FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation, headquartered in Tokyo, leverages its depth of knowledge and proprietary core technologies to deliver innovative products and services across the globe through the four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging with over 70,000 employees. Guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles,” we address social challenges and create a positive impact on society through our products, services, and business operations. Under its medium-term management plan, VISION2030, which ends in FY2030, we aspire to continue our evolution into a company that creates value and smiles for various stakeholders as a collection of global leading businesses and achieve a global revenue of 4 trillion yen (29 billion USD at an exchange rate of 140 JPY/USD). For more information, please visit: www.fujifilmholdings.com.

For further details about our commitment to sustainability and Fujifilm’s Sustainable Value Plan 2030, click here.

data.title: China's Home Prices Continued to Fall in August
data.description:
China's home prices continued to fall at a similar pace in August, remaining a key drag on the world's second-largest economy.

Home prices in 70 major Chinese cities dropped 0.17% in August from July, compared with July's 0.18% decline, according to calculations by The Wall Street Journal based on data from the National Bureau of Statistics on Tuesday.

Of the 70 cities, 49 reported declines in prices from the preceding month, the data showed.

When compared with a year earlier, home prices in these cities fell 3.3% in August, narrowing slightly from a 3.4% drop in July. Among them, 65 cities reported a year-over-year price declines in August.

In the first eight months of the year, home prices fell 3.5% on year.

China's property slump showed no sign of recovery, despite incremental government measures to ease home purchase restrictions, mortgage rules and down payment requirements.

data.title: Ukrainian Parliament Awards U.S. Bipartisan Delegation in Kyiv as Russian Attacks Intensify Against Civilian Infrastructure and the U.S. House Weighs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act
data.description:
Ukrainian Parliament Awards U.S. Bipartisan Delegation in Kyiv as Russian Attacks Intensify Against Civilian Infrastructure and the U.S. House Weighs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act

Ukrainian Parliament Awards U.S. Bipartisan Delegation in Kyiv as Russian Attacks Intensify Against Civilian Infrastructure and the U.S. House Weighs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Sept. 14, 2026

Three Republican senators and a bipartisan group of five U.S. representatives honored by Chairman Ruslan Stefanchuk; For Country Caucus backs the Russia sanctions bill as the House prepares to take up the Senate-passed version.

WASHINGTON, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine, Ruslan Stefanchuk, awarded the Ukrainian Badge of Honour "for our freedom and yours" to eight Members of Congress, including members of the For Country Caucus of bipartisan U.S. military veterans. The delegation traveled to Kyiv alongside the With Honor veterans organization for the Yalta European Strategy (YES) Annual Meeting, at a time of increased Russian attacks on civilians in the city. YES is one of the few international conferences that still convene annually in Ukraine.

The recipients were:

  • Sen. Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma
  • Sen. John Curtis of Utah
  • Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina
  • For Country Caucus Founding Co-Chair Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska's 2nd District
  • Former For Country Caucus Vice Chair Rep. Salud Carbajal of California's 24th District
  • Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Wesley Bell of Missouri's 1st District
  • Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Jim Costa of California's 21st District
  • Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Eugene Vindman of Virginia's 7th District

The award was also presented to With Honor Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and author of Courage Can Save US, which profiles Rep. Don Bacon and other bipartisan lawmakers who have served in the U.S. military or FBI and have demonstrated the courage to work across party lines on important national security issues, including the defense of Ukrainian freedom. With Honor led its fourth bipartisan delegation to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

In Kyiv, the delegation received briefings from senior Ukrainian officials, including Ukraine's National Security Advisor and Deputy Minister of Defense. Members passed gasoline stations and grocery stores in the capital that had been recently struck by Russian attacks. Part of the delegation also traveled to Kharkiv, where they met with frontline units and medics and saw additional destruction from Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure. As delegations departed Ukraine on Sunday, a Russian drone struck a train two kilometers from the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying officials out of Kyiv had passed through the same crossing. Ukraine's state rail operator said the diplomatic train may have been the intended target. No casualties were reported.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act passed the Senate on Aug. 7, 2026, by a bipartisan vote of 86-11. It is endorsed by With Honor Action and by the For Country Caucus, the bipartisan group of military veterans in the U.S. House that Rep. Bacon co-founded as its Republican co-chair and where Rep. Carbajal served as vice chair.

Separately, Congress appropriated $400 million for fiscal year 2026 for European capacity building, which the Department of Defense notified Congress it would use for Ukraine. The funds purchase weapons, equipment, and services from American manufacturers for Ukraine's armed forces. The Pentagon has not yet put those funds under contract. With Honor Action calls on the Administration to urgently obligate and disburse these funds in advance of the challenging winter Ukraine faces as it fights an enemy attacking civilian infrastructure.

"There is no substitute for standing in Kyiv while the sirens go off and watching people go about their day anyway. That is what resolve looks like. Ukraine is not asking Americans to fight this war. They are asking for the tools to finish it and for the pressure that brings Russia to the table honestly. The Senate did its part on sanctions last month, and I hope the House will finish the job this week," said Senator Thom Tillis, who led the Senate delegation.

"Twenty-five years ago this week, I was in uniform watching my country get hit. Marking that anniversary in Kyiv, in a city under fire from a dictator who treats borders as suggestions, sharpens what is at stake. We don't bow to dictators, and we don't leave a democracy to fight alone. This honor does not belong to the eight of us. It belongs to the American people who chose to arm a democracy under attack, and the way to honor it is to pass this sanctions bill and keep our commitments," said Rep. Don Bacon, who led the House delegation and is a retired U.S. Air Force brigadier general who was recently profiled in Barcott's book Courage Can Save US.

"My family left the Soviet Ukraine as refugees with almost nothing and were welcomed in America. My brothers and I gave back to our great nation by fighting for freedom in the U.S. military. We need to continue to fight for freedom by standing with Ukraine. This was my second trip as a Congressman, but the first trip where Kyiv was being hit while we were standing in it. The Ukrainians face a dire situation, and they were clear about their ask of America. They did not ask for American troops. They asked for pressure. The Senate passed this sanctions package 86 to 11, and every week the House waits is another week Russia sells the oil that pays for the missiles and drones whose damage we saw up close. The House should pass it this week," said Rep. Eugene Vindman, a retired Army colonel who serves on the House Armed Services Committee.

"Twenty-five years after 9/11, I marked the anniversary in a capital under fire alongside three Republican senators and a bipartisan group of five House members who traveled into a country under attack to stand with a democratic ally. We saw gas stations and grocery stores that Russia had struck days before, and met frontline medics in Kharkiv. On the way out, a drone hit the rail line minutes behind the train carrying officials from Kyiv, two kilometers from the Polish border," said Rye Barcott, Co-Founder and CEO of With Honor and a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. "Putin is escalating against civilians and testing NATO's edge. The Pentagon must put the $400 million Congress appropriated this year under contract without delay. That money buys weapons from American manufacturers, and every week of delay pushes delivery further out as Ukraine heads into winter. The Senate passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by a vote of 86 to 11. The House should take up that bill this week and send it to the President's desk."

About With Honor
With Honor fights polarization in Congress by supporting principled veterans across party lines who pledge to serve with integrity, civility, and courage. With Honor Action works alongside the bipartisan For Country Caucus in Congress to pass critical legislation for our nation. Learn more about our work at WithHonor.org.

Contact: press@withhonor.org

data.title: Peak3 launches the first global insurance AI-DLC, alongside its AI-native core system
data.description:
Peak3 launches the first global insurance AI-DLC, alongside its AI-native core system

Peak3 launches the first global insurance AI-DLC, alongside its AI-native core system

PR Newswire

SINGAPORE, Sept. 14, 2026

Graphene Harness turns insurance software delivery into an AI production line. Graphene v4 gives agents a governed core to run and change the business.

SINGAPORE, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak3, a global provider of digital and AI-driven insurance software, today announced Graphene v4, the AI-native evolution of its insurance core platform, and Graphene Harness, an end-to-end AI-driven delivery lifecycle (AI-DLC) for building, testing, migrating and maintaining insurance systems.

Insurance is among the most complex and heavily regulated industries, and among the slowest to change its software. That makes it one of the hardest tests of what AI can actually do. Graphene Harness is Peak3's answer: not AI applied to a single step of the work, but AI applied to the whole production line that builds and maintains the mission-critical systems and agents insurers run on.

Bill Song, CEO of Peak3: "We are disrupting ourselves. Peak3 is moving from selling software and related services to providing the production line that builds it — our entire AI-DLC."

Graphene v4: a governed core for agents across Life, P&C and Health

Graphene v4 includes the Graphene Agent Platform, a model-agnostic platform to build, run, observe and govern AI agents, with a marketplace of pre-built agents for tasks such as medical underwriting, conversational first notice of loss, intelligent document processing and fraud detection in claims. With v4, agents move beyond running the business to changing it: they (re-)configure insurance products, calculations and rules from unstructured documents and natural-language prompts, grounded in the insurer's own knowledge and data. Configuration work that traditionally takes days is completed in minutes to hours.

Graphene is open and headless by architecture. Every capability is exposed to agents through APIs, MCP and CLI, so an agent acts on the core directly instead of driving a user interface, under access management, strict attribution and detailed logging of every agent interaction, enforced at code level rather than through prompt-level guardrails.

Graphene v4 can also be deployed standalone, as a lightweight middle layer between AI agents and an insurer's existing systems of record. This gives insurers a fast route to agent-ready core capabilities without a complex core replacement.

Graphene v4 also widens functional breadth across all three major business lines: the complete group health lifecycle including provider network management; commercial lines with co-insurance and reinsurance administered inside the core; indexed universal life and crypto-denominated policies; and native Takaful support alongside conventional business.

Graphene Harness: the first global insurance AI-DLC

Graphene Harness is an end-to-end AI-driven delivery lifecycle for insurance software, built on a virtual scrum team model. Peak3 distilled the working knowledge of its most experienced staff into digital twins of every key delivery role — business analyst, architect, engineer, tester, reviewer — and connected every stage of the lifecycle into one governed system: agent teams running on an AI engineering platform, grounded in a curated knowledge base, and connected with AI-driven testing, migration, diagnostics and CI/CD.

Peak3 builds and maintains Graphene itself on Graphene Harness today. It is now being made available to selected implementation partners who deploy Graphene, and Peak3 intends to make it available to clients over the next 6 to 12 months. Alongside Graphene Harness, Peak3 is expanding its forward deployed engineering teams, who build AI-first operations alongside client teams across both Peak3 platforms and the client's existing stack.

What this changes for the insurance industry

Insurance IT cost has been anchored to headcount and elapsed time. An AI production line breaks that link: the same scope is delivered by a smaller team in a shorter cycle. Where Graphene Harness is applied, Peak3 is already achieving a 50% reduction in end-to-end new-feature development and core system implementation cost, with timelines reduced accordingly. Peak3's stated ambition is 80% within 18 to 36 months. An insurer using Graphene Harness also owns the means of changing its core system, rather than depending on a vendor's delivery organisation.

Additional detail on Graphene v4 and Graphene Harness is available in the Graphene v4 Release Highlights here . For more information, visit www.peak3.com.

About Peak3

Peak3 is a global provider of digital and AI-driven software solutions for the insurance industry. Specialising in AI-native core and orchestration platforms and innovative data and AI applications, Peak3 enables insurers, MGAs and intermediaries across life, health and P&C insurance to accelerate growth, enhance customer experience and improve operational efficiency. Headquartered in Singapore, Peak3 serves over 50 leading insurance clients in more than 20 countries across EMEA and APAC. Every year more than a billion policies get transacted on Peak3's solutions.

Peak3 is not affiliated, associated, authorised, endorsed by, or in any way connected with Peak Reinsurance Company Limited or any of its subsidiaries ("Peak Re").

data.title: RJK Explorations Ltd. Announces Closing of Previously Upsized Private Placement for Gross Proceeds of $150,000
data.description:
THIS NEWS RELEASE IS INTENDED FOR DISTRIBUTION IN CANADA ONLY AND IS NOT INTENDED FOR DISTRIBUTION TO UNITED STATES NEWSWIRE SERVICES OR DISSEMINATION IN THE UNITED STATES

KIRKLAND LAKE, ON / ACCESS Newswire / September 14, 2026 / RJK Explorations Ltd. (TSXV:RJX.A) (the "Company") is pleased to announce the closing of its previously upsized non-brokered private placement for gross proceeds of $150,000 (the "Offering"). The Offering consisted of the sale of 5,000,000 units (the "Units") of the Company at a price of $0.03 per Unit. Each Unit consists of one common share of the Company (a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant ("Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one Common Share at a price of $0.05 for a period of five years from the date of issuance. The Company intends to use 90% of the gross proceeds for exploration and development activities and 10% for working capital and general corporate purposes.

The Offering is subject to obtaining final approval of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). The securities issued pursuant to the Offering are subject to a four-month and one day hold period in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws and TSXV policies.

An insider of the Company purchased an aggregate of 1,666,667 Units pursuant to the Offering. The participation by such insider in the Offering constituted a "related party transaction" as defined under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company relied on exemptions from the formal valuation and minority approval requirements of sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 in respect of such insider participation, based on a determination that the fair market value of the participation in the Offering by such insider did not exceed 25% of the market capitalization of the Company, as determined in accordance with MI 61-101.

data.title: Dispatch Opens Its Wealth Operations Platform to the Industry With Launch of the Dispatch API
data.description:
Dispatch Opens Its Wealth Operations Platform to the Industry With Launch of the Dispatch API

Account opening is the first capability available, with Jump and Wealthbox among the first companies embedding Dispatch-powered custodian execution directly into their platforms

Dispatch, the data infrastructure platform that enables the wealth industry to run revenue-critical workflows, today announced the launch of the Dispatch API, which externalizes the company’s proven platform so wealthtech companies, fintech providers, and technology-forward registered investment advisors (RIAs) can embed its capabilities directly into their own products and workflows. Account opening is the first capability available via the Dispatch API, allowing companies to deliver essential custodian workflows within the technology experiences their customers already use, with additional capabilities coming soon.

Companies across wealth management technology increasingly want to own more of the workflows that sit on the critical path to revenue, but the infrastructure required to execute those workflows remains difficult and costly to build. Executing critical workflows requires companies to connect to fragmented custodian systems, standardize and reconcile financial data, validate it against complex requirements, orchestrate actions across multiple channels, and govern the entire process. The Dispatch API gives companies a way to adopt this infrastructure rather than build it internally, allowing them to focus their resources on the experiences and products they want to create.

“Dispatch has always been focused on making a firm’s data usable and turning that data into action,” said Rob Nance, co-founder and chief executive officer of Dispatch. “We proved that our platform can do this inside some of the largest RIAs in the country, supporting the operational workflows that directly drive revenue for their businesses. The Dispatch API is the next chapter of that story: opening the infrastructure we have already built so other companies can bring execution into their own products without having to recreate it themselves.”

Technology-driven experiences are becoming the new wedge for advisory firms to earn more, and earn sooner. As wealthtech companies race to transform the advisor and client experience, the Dispatch API gives them the infrastructure to bring their ideas to life – allowing them to run operational workflows behind whatever experience they can imagine. That requires more than a simple API connection. Dispatch’s platform brings together five critical layers: the translation layer, the ontology, the firm graph, agentic action, and the audit and control pane. Together, these layers enable technology companies to translate data across systems, understand the relationships and context within a firm, take action across operational workflows, and maintain the controls and auditability required to execute revenue-critical work. The Dispatch API makes these capabilities available to companies building the next generation of wealth technology, with account opening as the starting point.

Jump and Wealthbox are the first two software companies leveraging the Dispatch API to embed account opening directly into the technology experiences advisors already use. Each integration demonstrates how Dispatch can power custodian execution from a different starting point in the advisor workflow.

Through Jump, the leading AI (artificial intelligence) platform for advisors and financial services professionals, an advisor can open a custodian account live with the client on the call, turning a process that used to take hours into minutes. Jump turns the client conversation into an end-to-end account-opening workflow. It combines what the client shares live with information the firm already has, validates the application against custodian requirements through Dispatch and gets it signed before the meeting ends. From conversation to submitted paperwork, nothing is re-entered and no work is handed off between disconnected systems, freeing advisors and home-office capacity for more clients.

“Advisors should not have to leave the conversation, reenter information across multiple systems and manually initiate the next step for a client,” said Parker Ence, co-founder and chief executive officer of Jump. “By building on the Dispatch API, we’re enabling real-time account opening directly from the advisor workflow, connecting the intelligence captured during a client meeting with the infrastructure needed to execute that next step. This creates a more seamless experience for advisors and their clients, while relying on Dispatch to manage the complexity of custodian validation and execution behind the scenes.”

Through Wealthbox, an advisor can open an account directly from the client record already in front of them, using the data the customer relationship management (CRM) already holds. Wealthbox supplies the client information required to initiate the account-opening process, while Dispatch validates the data, confirms the account meets custodian requirements, routes the submission through the appropriate channel and tracks its progress through funding.

“Every account opening starts with the client information already living in Wealthbox, the source of truth advisors rely on,” said John Rourke, co-founder and chief executive officer of Wealthbox. “Building on the Dispatch API means that information does not have to be copied into a separate system to get an account opened. Dispatch takes what is already accurate in the CRM and carries it through custodian validation and execution, so the advisor’s next step is confirming, not retyping.”

The Dispatch platform is already used by half of the ten largest RIAs for account opening and advisor transitions. Tens of billions of dollars in assets have moved through Dispatch rails across hundreds of thousands of accounts opened, establishing Dispatch as a proven solution for opening accounts at major U.S. custodians. Additional platform capabilities will become available via the Dispatch API over time.

To learn more, visit Dispatch.io.

About Dispatch

Dispatch provides the operational infrastructure powering revenue critical workflows for modern wealth management firms. The platform connects the industry's leading custodians—including Fidelity, Charles Schwab, and Pershing—with the core systems firms rely on every day. With Dispatch, firms can seamlessly open accounts, transition advisors, and sync data across CRMs, planning, billing, eSignature and document management platforms.

By unifying workflows across the wealth management ecosystem, Dispatch helps firms accelerate AUM, streamline their most important workflows, and drive increased revenue.

For more information, follow Dispatch on LinkedIn or visit dispatch.io.

About Jump

Jump is the leading AI platform for financial services professionals, trusted by firms of all sizes — including LPL Financial, Osaic Wealth, Cetera Financial Group, Equitable, Allianz, Manulife and Principal Financial Group. Built for the entire client lifecycle, Jump helps firms elevate every interaction, onboard clients in minutes and grow their business through tailored insights and automated workflows. Ranked #1 in advisor satisfaction and adoption by T3, Kitces and The Oasis Group, Jump sets the standard for compliant AI. Learn more at jump.ai.

About Wealthbox

Wealthbox® is an AI-powered CRM platform for financial advisors. Integrated with leading custodians and wealthtech partners, Wealthbox is recognized for its modern product design and powerful yet intuitive user experience. The platform enables financial advisors, enterprise RIA firms, and broker-dealers to effectively manage client relationships, streamline operations, and turn years of practice data into intelligent action. Learn more at www.wealthbox.com.

data.title: Shanghai Electric Reports 16.6% Revenue Growth in H1 2026 as New Orders Reach CNY 100.39 Billion
data.description:
Shanghai Electric Reports 16.6% Revenue Growth in H1 2026 as New Orders Reach CNY 100.39 Billion

Shanghai Electric Reports 16.6% Revenue Growth in H1 2026 as New Orders Reach CNY 100.39 Billion

PR Newswire

SHANGHAI, Sept. 14, 2026

Accelerated deployment of green energy and industrial AI technologies, with project progress in European and Middle Eastern markets

SHANGHAI, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shanghai Electric (SEHK: 02727, SSE: 601727) has released its interim results for the first half of 2026. During the reporting period, it achieved operating revenue of CNY 63.332 billion (USD 9.17 billion), up 16.6% year‑on‑year; net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company reached CNY 970 million (USD 140.49 million), an increase of 18.2%; and new orders totaled CNY 100.39 billion (USD 14.54 billion), marking further progress in energy transition, high‑end intelligent manufacturing, and international expansion.

Sustained momentum across three business pillars, with orders providing long‑term visibility

Shanghai Electric's Energy Equipment segment posted revenue of CNY 36.558 billion (USD 5.29 billion), up 21.4% year‑on‑year, driven by growth in its wind power and energy storage businesses. The Industrial Equipment segment generated CNY 18.954 billion (USD 2.75 billion) in revenue, a 1.9% increase, as digital and smart technologies reinforced its position in machine tools, elevators, and industrial components. The Integrated Services segment achieved revenue of CNY 10.862 billion (USD 1.57 billion), up 31.5%. The segment continued to strengthen its capabilities in supply chain coordination, customized solutions, and full-lifecycle services.

Of the new orders, Energy Equipment accounted for CNY 64.24 billion (USD 9.30 billion)—including CNY 12.39 billion (USD 1.79 billion) for wind power equipment, CNY 11.44 billion (USD 1.66 billion) for energy storage equipment, CNY 4.57 billion (USD 661.91 million) for nuclear power equipment, and CNY 20.23 billion (USD 2.93 billion) for coal‑fired power generation equipment. New orders for Industrial Equipment and Integrated Services stood at CNY 21.25 billion (USD 3.08 billion) and CNY 14.91 billion (USD 2.16 billion), respectively.

Advancing overseas project expansion and localized operations

During the reporting period, Shanghai Mitsubishi Elevator secured the contract for the Dubai Palm Island Phase II project, supplying 700 high-end elevators and related services.

Marking its first large-scale entry into Europe's high-end market, Shanghai Electric's power transmission and distribution business won a contract to supply high- and low-voltage switchgear for a hyperscale data center in Finland.

The company also signed a contract for the Minety Phase II Stonehill Energy Storage Project (50 MW/150 MWh) in the UK, further reinforcing its strategic footprint in the European premium energy storage market.

Shanghai Electric has established a "1+N+6" international business management network, with newly opened regional headquarters in Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa driving global business synergy and strengthening localized operations across key markets.

Technology- and innovation- driven strategy breaks new ground in green energy and high-end manufacturing

In green fuels, the company's proprietary "green power + biomass gasification to green methanol" full‑chain technology, validated in Jilin's Taonan project, has secured the EPC contract for the Lanzhou New Area 100,000‑ton/year biomass green methanol project (Phase I), now under construction.

In new energy and high‑end equipment, the company has mastered key nuclear equipment manufacturing and testing technologies, with offshore wind orders exceeding 2 GW. The company also contributed to the full commissioning of the Huai'an Salt Cavern Compressed Air Energy Storage Project—the world's largest.

In industrial intelligence, the "SUYUAN 2.0" humanoid robot made its domestic debut, with over 40 AI agents deployed across R&D, production, and maintenance. The SEunicloud Industrial Internet Platform has connected about 1.16 million devices and developed over 60 industry‑specific digital solutions.

Looking ahead, Shanghai Electric will focus on coordination and efficiency, international expansion, and digitalization to advance the high-end, intelligent, green, and integrated development of its businesses.
